verses.38:16: Desde a manhã até a tarde {finies2}: * como o filhote da andorinha, assim clamarei, {meditabor} como a pomba:

decisions.latin: ad portas ínferi · non inférnus confitébitur tibi
decisions.why: The glossary's row *inférnus / ínferi → inferno* (open, for Gustavo) covers both words; its genitive precedent is 48:16 and 88:49 *de manu ínferi → da mão do inferno*, and 9:15 / 106:18 give *portas da morte* for the parallel *portæ mortis*. The only other place with the same two Latin words, Mt 16:18 *portæ inferi*, is *as forças do Inferno* even in the modern CNBB Bible (fetched). The separate open row *ad ínferos* (canticle 212) is about the accusative plural after a verb of motion, where 212 kept the plural *aos infernos*; here the Latin is a genitive after *portas*, which the psalter has always said in the singular. 38:22 *inférnus* (nominative singular) is the row's word, as in 6:6 *no inferno … quem vos dará graças?* — which this verse echoes. The risk, as in every place of the row: the ear hears the hell of the damned first; the Brazilian LH and Lectionary paraphrase both places as *a mansão triste dos mortos*.

options.label: do inferno · o inferno
options.note: Draft. The row's word; the psalter's genitive (48:16, 88:49); 6:6 for 38:22. DRB *the gates of hell … hell shall not confess to thee*.

options.label: dos infernos · o inferno
options.note: Canticle 212's plural for *ínferi*; it would mark the Latin's plural here, but split the genitive from 48:16 and 88:49, and 38:22 (singular) could not follow.

options.label: da morada dos mortos · a morada dos mortos
options.note: The row's option for a realm-of-the-dead reading. A paraphrase of one word by three; it would have to go into the whole row, not one canticle.

options.label: da mansão dos mortos · a mansão dos mortos
options.note: The Creed's and the CNBB LH / Lectionary's words (*para a mansão triste dos mortos descerei*; circulation.md). Same objection: a paraphrase, and a ruling for the whole row.

decisions.why: The same four Latin words stand in 101:25 *Ne révoces me in dimídio diérum meórum → Não me chameis de volta no meio dos meus dias*; rule 6 copies them. MS1932 *Na metade de meus dias*, DRB *In the midst of my days*; the LH paraphrases *no apogeu de minha vida*.

options.label: Na metade dos meus dias
options.note: MS1932. The half, closer to *dimídium*; but it would part the canticle from 101:25.

decisions.why: The perfect, twice. The psalter's *Ego dixi* is *Eu disse* (40:5, 81:6, 115:2), and bare *dixi* in 141:6 and 54:7 is *eu disse*, the pronoun supplied so that the Portuguese is not heard as 'he said'. The LH and the Lectionary say *Eu dizia* (the imperfect of inner speech, which is how this song is usually read: 'I used to think'). The perfect is the Latin's tense; D2 lets the ear lead on grammar, but here the perfect is not strained.

options.label: Eu dizia … Eu dizia
options.note: The LH and Lectionary wording Brazilian ears know. It interprets the tense.

decisions.why: Jerome's *quæsívi* ('I sought') is not the Hebrew (*puqqadtî*, 'I am deprived of'); the Latin is translated as it stands (DRB *I sought for the residue of my years*; MS1932 *Busquei o resto de meus anos*, with his note that the dying man 'would have wanted to hold it back'). Whether the words still belong to what was 'said' in 38:10 is left open, as the Latin leaves it: no quotation marks. *Quǽrere → buscar* (the glossary). *Resíduum*: *o resto* is plain and exact.

options.label: Busquei o resto dos meus anos

forms.quaesivi: Busquei o resto dos meus anos

options.label: Busquei o que resta dos meus anos

forms.quaesivi: Busquei o que resta dos meus anos

options.note: The LH's *o que me resta dos meus anos* (a paraphrase of another text) gives the turn; a clause for a noun.

options.label: Procurei o resto dos meus anos

forms.quaesivi: Procurei o resto dos meus anos

decisions.latin: Non aspíciam hóminem ultra, * et habitatórem
decisions.why: The glossary's *aspícere → olhar para* (65:18; open) keeps it apart from *vidébo → verei* in the verse before; MS1932 and the LH merge them (*Não verei mais homem algum*; *nunca mais verei um homem*). *Et* after a negative becomes *nem* (grammar). *Hóminem* stays the bare generic noun, *o homem*.

options.label: olharei mais para … para o
options.note: Draft; the row's verb, and the preposition repeated so that both objects hang on it.

options.label: verei mais … o
options.note: MS1932 and DRB (*behold*). Merges two Latin verbs one line apart.

decisions.why: Obscure in the Latin, as in the Hebrew (Jerome read *ḥedel*, 'cessation', as rest). Who is 'the dweller of rest' — the living at peace, or the dead at rest — the Latin does not say; it stays open. *Quies* has not met the psalter; *réquies → repouso* (94:10, 131:5–14) is the nearest row, and one root for the pair is right (L&S: *quies* rest, quiet; *requies* rest). MS1932 *nem habitante do repouso*; DRB *nor the inhabitant of rest*.

*Generátio → geração* is the psalter's word (the glossary; 144:4, 101:13 …). Here it is 'my age, my lifetime' — DRB *My generation is at an end*; MS1932 paraphrases *Foi-me tirado o tempo da minha vida*; the LH follows the Hebrew *dôr* read as 'dwelling' (*Minha morada foi … arrebatada*), which the Latin does not say. *Geração* keeps the Latin's word and its reach (a man's span of life is his *generátio*), at the cost of a moment's puzzlement. *Auférre → tirar* (D41).

options.label: idade
options.note: An interpretation (lifetime) in one plain word; L&S gives 'an age' for *generatio*.

options.label: morada
options.note: The Hebrew and the LH. Refused: not the Latin's sense (rule 1).

decisions.why: *Convólvere* is to roll up (L&S), and *a me* is 'away from me' — a tent struck and rolled up, as the second colon says. The participle is kept under the first *foi*; *para longe de* supplies what the preposition *a* carries.

options.label: foi enrolada e tirada de mim

forms.convoluta: foi enrolada e tirada de mim

options.note: Doubles *tirar*, which the Latin says once.

options.label: enrolou-se longe de mim
options.note: MS1932's reflexive (*ela se me enrolou*); breaks the Latin's pair of passives.

decisions.why: Two verbs of cutting. DO's accent (*succídit*) makes it *succīdo* < *sub-cædo*, 'to cut from below, cut down, fell; to mow, reap' (L&S), not *succĭdo* 'sink'. *Præcídere* 'cut off' takes *cortar*, the weaving image of the colon (*cortada como por um tecelão*). For *succídere* *ceifar* is the cut from below, and *ceifar a vida* is living Brazilian speech for a death; it keeps the Latin's two verbs apart. MS1932 *ele ma cortou*, DRB *he cut me off* merge them. The subject is not named, as in the Latin.

options.label: ceifou-me
options.note: Draft. Distinct from *cortar*; a reaping image laid over the weaving one, which L&S's *succido* allows.

options.label: cortou-me
options.note: MS1932, DRB. Plainest; makes a repetition (*cortada … cortou-me*) the Latin does not have.

options.label: abateu-me
options.note: 'Felled me' — but *abater* is heard first as 'discouraged me'.

decisions.latin: de mane usque ad vésperam fínies me
decisions.why: The line repeats word for word (38:14, 38:16), and so does the Portuguese. *Fínies me* turns suddenly to God (second person, future): 'you will make an end of me' (DRB). MS1932 *tu acabarás comigo*; the glossary's *consummáre* (a person) → *acabar com* (118:87) is the same idiom. *Vesper → tarde* (103:23 *até a tarde*).

options.label: dareis fim a mim
options.note: Keeps *finis* audible; heavier, and ends on the oxytone *mim* as *comigo* does not.

decisions.why: *Meditári → meditar* is the glossary's (1:2, 2:1, 62:7, 76:13). Here it is the dove's murmur (the Hebrew *hāgâ* is to moan, coo), which the Latin verb holds (L&S *meditor*: to think over, but *meditari* in the Vulgate often renders the low sound of *hāgâ*). DRB keeps *I will meditate like a dove*; MS1932 *gemia como a pomba*; the LH *o meu gemido*. The Latin's word is kept; the image of sound is lost to a reader who does not know it.

options.label: gemerei
options.note: MS1932's sense and the LH's. It explains the verb from the Hebrew; *gemere* is another Latin word.

decisions.why: *Attenuáre*: to make thin or weak (L&S). The psalter's eyes that fail are *defecérunt → desfaleceram* (68:4, 118:82) and *languérunt → se enfraqueceram* (87:9b); *infirmári → enfraquecer* too. A third Latin verb, so a third Portuguese: *definhar* is to grow thin and waste away. DRB *weakened*; MS1932 and the LH *cansaram-se* (another sense, *laboráre → cansar-se*, 68:4).

Two rows meet: *in excélso → no alto* (72:8, 72:11) and the noun *excélsum → altura* (101:20 *de excélso sancto suo → da sua santa altura*). Here it is a direction after *in* + accusative, as 72:8's is a place after *in* + ablative; *para o alto* follows 72:8 and is what MS1932, DM1962 and the LH all say. *Suspícere* (look up) → *olhar* with the direction.

*Cum* with the perfect subjunctive, 'when/since he himself has done it' (DRB *whereas he himself hath done it*; MS1932 *quando ele mesmo é que fez isto*). *Ipse fecit → ele mesmo o fez* is the psalter's formula (94:5, 99:3a); the object *o* is supplied, as there. *Quando* keeps *cum*'s range (time shading into cause); *se* would make it a condition, *pois* would close it to cause.

options.label: se foi ele mesmo que o fez

forms.cumipse: se foi ele mesmo que o fez

options.note: Idiomatic ('seeing that'); longer, and *se* is heard as 'if'.

decisions.why: *Recogitáre*: to think over again, reflect upon (L&S). *Repassar* is exactly 'go over again' and is MS1932's verb (*Repassarei diante de ti pela memória*). The dative *tibi* → *diante de vós* (MS1932) is a preposition the ear accepts; *para vós* is the bare dative and sounds like a gift. *Cogitáre → pensar em* is the glossary's, so *repensar* would keep the root but means 'reconsider'.

options.label: Recordarei para vós
options.note: DRB *recount to thee*; *recordári* is another Latin verb.

decisions.latin: Ecce, in pace amaritúdo mea amaríssima
decisions.why: A verbless line, famously open. It can be read (a) 'in the time of peace my bitterness is most bitter' (Bernard's reading, applied to the Church at peace) or (b) 'my most bitter bitterness is (turned) into peace' (nearer the Hebrew, 'for peace I had great bitterness'). DRB supplies *is* (*in peace is my bitterness most bitter*) and keeps both; MS1932 resolves (*Encontrarei paz na minha amargosíssima aflição*). *Eis* + a noun phrase is good Portuguese (*Eis o homem*) and adds no verb, so the Latin's openness stands. The Latin's play *amaritúdo … amaríssima* is kept as closely as Portuguese allows: *amargura … amaríssima* (the learned superlative of *amargo*). The ambiguity reader should say whether *amaríssima* is understood.

options.label: Eis, em paz, a minha amargura amaríssima

forms.inpace: Eis, em paz, a minha amargura

options.label: Eis que em paz é a minha amargura amaríssima

forms.inpace: Eis que em paz é a minha amargura

options.label: Eis que se tornou paz a minha amargura amaríssima

forms.inpace: Eis que se tornou paz a minha amargura

options.note: Reading (b), spelled out. Refused: it closes what the Latin leaves open.

decisions.why: The superlative of *amárus*. Portuguese has the learned *amaríssimo* and the popular *amarguíssimo*; the first keeps the Latin's word, the second keeps the root of *amargura* (the Latin's echo *amaritúdo … amaríssima*). Both end on a proparoxytone, as the Latin does at the mediant.

options.label: mais amarga
options.note: Plain; gives up the superlative's form.

decisions.why: The Latin's repetition is kept (rule 2). *Vivens* as a person: 38:6b *omnis homo vivens → todo homem que vive*; 142:2 *omnis vivens → nenhum vivente*. MS1932 *O que vive, o que vive, esse é o que te louvará*. *Ipse* resumes the subject → *esse*.

options.label: O que vive, o que vive

forms.vivens: O que vive, o que vive

options.label: Quem vive, quem vive
options.note: Lighter; *quem* sits less well with the resumptive *esse*.

choices.38:10: DO's first line, *(Canticum Ezechiæ \* Isa 38:10-24)*, is a heading with a book reference, not a prayed verse and not a titulus; readVerses skips it, as for 233, 211, 213, and D7 keeps it untranslated. For delivery to DO, its Portuguese heading can be *(Cântico de Ezequias \* Is 38:10-24)*. DO's ids 38:10–38:24 are the canticle's own line numbers; the text is Isa 38:10–20 of the Vulgate (map at the head of `consult/parallels/ps222.md`). The Latin is Jerome's Isaiah, from the Hebrew, not the Gallican psalter; where the Hebrew is obscure and Jerome read it otherwise (38:11 *quæsívi*, 38:12 *quiétis*, 38:13 *generátio*, 38:20 *in pace*), the Latin is translated as it stands. *Vadam* → *irei* (DRB *I shall go*; MS1932 *irei*). The Latin has no quotation marks and neither does the Portuguese: where Hezekiah's remembered words end is left as open as the Latin leaves it.
choices.38:11: *Dóminum Deum* → *o Senhor Deus*. *In terra vivéntium* → *na terra dos vivos*, the formula of 26:13, 51:7 and 141:6 (the LH's *terra dos viventes* not taken).
choices.38:12: *Ultra* → *mais* after the verb (82:5 *non memorétur … ultra → não seja mais lembrado*).
choices.38:13: *Tabernáculum → tenda* (the glossary). *Quasi tabernáculum pastórum* → *como uma tenda de pastores* (MS1932's words; the plural *pastórum* kept against the LH's *de um pastor*).
choices.38:14: DO marks this verse with the mediant only (no flex); DO's pointing is followed. The order is Portuguese (*A minha vida foi cortada*); the Latin fronts the verb. *Velut a texénte → como por um tecelão* (MS1932). *Dum adhuc ordírer → enquanto eu ainda urdia*: *ordíri* is to lay the warp, begin a web (L&S), and *urdir* is its Portuguese; the weaving image stays whole. The first colon is long (the Latin's is too, ~27 syllables), with a natural breath at the colon.
choices.38:15: *Sperábam* → *Eu esperava* (the *speráre* row without its *in*; no object in the Latin). DO's comma before the mediant becomes a colon, so that *até a manhã* is not read with *como um leão*. *Contérere → quebrar* (3:8, 104:16, 106:16). *Quasi leo sic* → *como um leão, assim*, both words kept; the subject of *contrívit* is not named, as in the Latin.
choices.38:16: The first colon is 38:14's second, word for word. *Pullus → filhote* (the glossary; 83:4). *Clamábo → clamarei*; *colúmba → pomba* (54:7).
choices.38:17: Eight and eight syllables against eleven and nine; the Latin's words are long, the line is not thin.
choices.38:18: *Vim pátior → sofro violência* (37:12b *vim faciébant → faziam violência*). *Respónde* → *respondei* — the *vós* imperative of an *-er* verb, not the homograph of *respondi* (rule 3). The person shifts from *vós* (God, addressed) to *ele* (God, spoken of: *ipse*), as the Latin does; kept.
choices.38:20: The antiphon DO draws from this verse (Tuesday Lauds II: *Corrípies me, Dómine, \* et vivificábis me*) can be said as *Vós me castigareis, Senhor, \* e me vivificareis*. *Corrípere → castigar* (D21); *vivificáre → vivificar* (137:7, 142:11a *vós me vivificareis*). *Si sic vívitur* → *se assim se vive* (the impersonal passive as the Portuguese impersonal). The verbless *et in tálibus vita spíritus mei* takes a supplied *se … está* (the *si* governs both clauses; grammar). The subject *vós* is named because the preceding verse ended in the third person (*ipse*). DO has no flex in this verse, so the long first colon (the Latin's is 32 syllables) keeps its one breath at the comma after *espírito*.
choices.38:21: *Tu autem → Vós, porém* (3:4, 39:12, 101:13). *Éruere* without a source → *libertar* (the row's rule: 6:5 *éripe ánimam meam → libertai a minha alma*, 68:19, 118:153); the Lectionary's refrain says *livrastes*, which is *liberáre*'s. *Ut non períret → para que não perecesse*. *Projícere → lançar* (30:23, 49:17 *lançaste para trás*); *post tergum tuum → para trás das vossas costas* (MS1932, with *tergum* the back).
choices.38:22: *Confitéri → dar graças a* (D5), *laudáre → louvar*, *exspectáre → aguardar* (D24, D36), *descendéntes in lacum → os que descem à cova* (the *lacus* formula: 27:1, 29:4, 87:5, 142:7b), *véritas → verdade*. The Latin fronts *non inférnus* and ends on *veritátem tuam*; the Portuguese keeps the object at the end (*a vossa verdade*), which is where the Latin has it.
choices.38:23: *Sicut et ego hódie → como também eu hoje*: *et* = also. *Notam fácere → fazer conhecer* (the glossary; 76:15, 105:8, 144:12 *para fazerem conhecer aos filhos dos homens*). *Pater fíliis* → *o pai … aos filhos*.
choices.38:24: *Salvum me fac → salvai-me* (the formula). *Psalmos … cantábimus → cantaremos os nossos salmos*: here the Latin itself says *cantáre psalmos*, so *entoar salmos* (D25, for *psállere*) is not wanted. *Cunctis diébus vitæ nostræ → todos os dias da nossa vida* (22:6, 26:4, 127:5 for *ómnibus diébus*, with *meæ/tuæ*; the Latin's two words for 'all' meet no Portuguese pair). *In domo Dómini → na casa do Senhor*. The mediant colon is short (5 against 7): the formula; the antiphon *Cunctis diébus vitæ nostræ salvos nos fac, Dómine* (Tuesday Lauds, 1911 and Monastic) can be said as *Todos os dias da nossa vida salvai-nos, Senhor*.

audit.note: Canticle-level draft. parallels.py handles psalm numbers only, so ps222/show_parallels.py builds consult/parallels/ps222.md from the Bolls Vulgate, Douay-Rheims and WLC Hebrew of Isa 38 (consult/ps222/bolls-*-23-38.json), the Rahlfs LXX (consult/lxx-*.csv; a freer text, distant here), Matos Soares 1932 (pdftotext -layout of the 1932 PDF, printed pp. 481–482, consult/ps222/ms1932-isa38-p481-482.txt) and the Diurnal Monástico 1962 (Tuesday Lauds, from the Hebrew-family text). All third-party files are under consult/ (gitignored), none in ps222/. Precedent checked with ps222/concord.py (a copy of ps213's): 101:25 *in dimídio diérum meórum*, 48:16 / 88:49 *ínferi*, 9:15 / 106:18 *portas da morte*, the *lacus* formula, 94:5 *ele mesmo o fez*, 137:7 *vós me vivificareis*, 144:12 *fazer conhecer*. Brazilian circulation fetched into ps222/circulation.md (CNBB LH Tuesday Lauds II, Is 38,10-14.17-20, a paraphrase; the Lectionary's responsorial on Friday of the 15th week, year II, with the same text; Mt 16:18 in the CNBB Bible). Hard readings: 38:13 *generátio … convolúta a me*, 38:14 the two verbs of cutting, 38:20 *in pace amaritúdo mea amaríssima*, 38:12 *habitatórem quiétis*.

render.py and checks.py with 222: hard checks pass (ids 38:10–38:24 and every * match; the canticle has no † or ‡). Soft flags kept: 38:10a −5 and 38:11a −4 (the Latin's long words; *No meio dos meus dias* is 101:25's formula); 38:14 and 38:16 +4/+5 (*acabareis comigo* for *fínies me*, and the weaving colon; the Latin's own colons are long); 38:17a −3; 38:20a +6 (the supplied *se … está* and the named *vós*); 38:12b and 38:21a +3. Cadences: 38:15a ends oxytone (*manhã*); all colons end paroxytone or oxytone except 38:20b's proparoxytone *amaríssima*, which matches the Latin's. The -ade rhyme 38:22/38:23 is the Latin's own repetition of *veritátem tuam*; not sought, kept. Precedents re-verified with concord.py after drafting (6:5, 68:19, 118:153 for *éripe* without a source; 105:8 for *notam fácere*; 22:6, 26:4, 127:5).
